issue_context.title: The global index not work with `memIndexReader` executor
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
CREATE TABLE `t` (
  `a` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `b` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `c` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`a`) /*T![clustered_index] CLUSTERED */,
  UNIQUE KEY `idx1` (`b`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
PARTITION BY HASH (`a`) PARTITIONS 5;
insert into t values (2, 2, 3), (3, 4, 5), (4, 5, 6);
begin;
insert into t values (5, 6, 7);
select b from t where b >= 2;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```
mysql> select b from t where b >= 2;
+------+
| b    |
+------+
|    2 |
|    4 |
|    5 |
|    6 |
+------+
3 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
mysql> select b from t where b >= 2;
+------+
| b    |
+------+
|    6 |
+------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
comments:
Caused by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/41992/files#diff-d73d3a1acc55230180db0c3b4fbd89bead84e15845062549e20ec9e810a283b9R330, maybe we should move the add `SelectionExec` part code to planner part.

And also this PR didn't fix `Selection` problem in `UnionScanExec`. Like

```
mysql> select b from t partition(p1) use index(idx1); -- The result should be empty.
+------+
| b    |
+------+
|    6 |
+------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

review_comments: Is this only for when we have changed data in this transaction, but reading from the global index with explicit partitioning selection `... from t partition (p0,...)` or is it needed for other cases as well?
filter adding and dropping partitions also need this map.
hard to get, pls add some comments about this
Done

Should the expression just be 'false' or simply evaluate to 'false' instead if there are no matching partition?
Or are there any way to say that this data source will always return zero rows and avoid even execute it?
TableDual is such data source
I don't know is it reasonable to generate a tableDual here? /cc @qw4990 @AilinKid
Maybe add a comment that the Adding/DroppingDefinitions cannot be part of this? At least I had to think about it :)
Done

If partition pruning fail, then `err != nil`. We'll not add the Selection, will this cause the wrong data returned?
And may other error happen and ignored here?
Not sure, but https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/52660/files/5343d4eb1dab5f57b431403234ad6f7f9df7cbee#diff-e82acde450b380d2b2347aeb83d34bffaaa10b19d9eb24ea7aadbef96d71c875R1246 also return a nil
/cc @qw4990 @AilinKid
Added a log here and the return nil means the innerPlan is empty. So I think no wrong data will returned.
when the returned task is nil, it means the buildTaskForInner is failed. other alternatives will be chooses except this, it's ok
What does `len(is.ByItems) != 0` mean? Does it no longer need partitioning pruning?

`partitionIDMap` only used in `unionScan` with global index. I added it before, but I thinking `is.ByItems` is useless right now. Because https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/52660/files#diff-d5994c60aa9e9c4233087811556f65e4e37d6af33176dc2bfe64e4569211d300L1107 is deleted.
Same here, any other use case than explicit partition selection?
ditto
There can be multiple extra 'hidden' columns, are we sure that there are non of the others? (TODO: find their definition...)
Can you please explain the difference between `len(tps)-1` and `len(m.index.Columns)`?

Here we need to confirm whether intHandle is `unsigned` or `signed`, `len(tps)-1` always return the last one. But when we add some hidden columns, the last column not always related with handle.

The distribution of column is like this
```
| some index columns | handle columns | hidden columns |
```
why move all the existence check away?
Because it couldn't failed, if table has a global index, it should be a partition table.
@tiancaiamao should we add this? Looks a little bit weird.
In `selection`, normal partition IDs are also numbers, and -1 feels fine for me.
Should we add a check that `len(args) == 1` after this?
Done
